content: The Pennsylvania College of Optometry (PCO) is one of the oldest institutions dedicated to the field of optometry. Throughout much of the 20th century, it has been a leader in both optometric education and research. It was the first school in the United States to award the Doctor of Optometry degree following a four-year educational program. Additionally, it was the first optometry school to achieve regional accreditation and the first to introduce courses specifically focused on contact lenses. PCO pioneered interdisciplinary clinical training and established off-campus externship programs, providing students with diverse clinical experiences. It was also the first independent optometry college to develop graduate programs in vision rehabilitation and to affiliate with a medical school. Furthermore, PCO was the first to revise its curriculum to integrate basic and clinical courses using a modular approach, introducing clinical concepts, skills, and patient interaction early in the educational program rather than as an additional phase after completing foundational studies. The Eye Institute (TEI) serves as the primary clinical facility for PCO. Since its inception, TEI has been recognized globally as a premier clinical center. It offers a wide range of services, including adult primary care, pediatric care, vision rehabilitation, laser procedures, subspecialty optometry services, and subspecialty ophthalmology services. This state-of-the-art training facility operates 24 hours a day, and all PCO graduates gain hands-on experience at TEI early in their studies. Within The Eye Institute is the William Feinbloom Vision Rehabilitation Center, which specializes in low vision care and attracts patients from around the world. It remains the leading research center for low vision globally. In addition to TEI, PCO operates two other clinical facilities in the Philadelphia area and administers one of the largest externship programs in the country. This program allows optometry students to rotate through various clinical settings, including private practices, clinics, government facilities, veterans’ hospitals, and Indian reservation clinics under the Department of the Interior, ensuring graduates receive a broad spectrum of clinical experience. In 1929, Henry W. Breyer purchased the abandoned Lindenhurst property, formerly owned by John Wanamaker, in Cheltenham on York Road, below Washington Lane. Breyer later donated this land to the Boy Scouts of America for use as a wildlife preserve. The site, known as Camp Henry W. Breyer, was sold by the Philadelphia Council in 1990 and is now home to the Pennsylvania College of Optometry. The Elkins Park Campus of PCO is situated on 11 acres of land in Cheltenham Township, approximately three miles from The Eye Institute, which serves as the College's clinical classroom in West Oak Lane. The Elkins Park Campus features first-class amenities and includes a man-made pond, which has been humorously described as resembling a 2000 Flushes Blue toilet bowl due to its treated appearance.
